primary_meaning: direction of divine glory/presence, paradise (Eden), light, and the coming/advent of Christ (rising sun/resurrection)
primary_basis: Genesis 2:8 (Lord God planted a garden in Eden, in the east)
Genesis 3:24 (cherubim and flaming sword east of the garden of Eden)
Ezekiel 43:1-5 (glory of the God of Israel came from the east; the earth shone with his glory)
Malachi 4:2 (sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings)
Matthew 2:1-2 (wise men from the east... we saw his star when it rose)
Matthew 24:27 (as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man)

alternatives.meaning: source of destructive judgment or scorching/desolating force (especially the east wind)
basis: Exodus 14:21 (east wind drove the sea back)
Hosea 13:15 (east wind... shall come, a wind of the Lord, rising from the wilderness)
Jonah 4:8 (God appointed a scorching east wind)

alternatives.meaning: direction of exile, foreign empires, or distant/pagan lands (Babylon and beyond)
basis: Genesis 11:2 (people migrated from the east and settled in Shinar)
Isaiah 2:6 / 46:11 (influences or a bird of prey from the east)

alternatives.meaning: place of wisdom or seekers who recognize the true King (Magi typology)
basis: Matthew 2:1-12 (Magi from the east following the star to worship)

notes: Biblical and traditional Christian usage of 'East' is strongly contextual rather than univocal; the dominant liturgical and interpretive association (ad orientem prayer, church orientation, paradise/glory/Christ as rising sun) is well-attested and widely recognized across patristic, medieval, and modern sources, while meteorological/geopolitical negative senses remain common but secondary. No single exclusive meaning exists, yet a clear primary positive cluster is the settled consensus in Christian symbolism.
